The drop came despite the sizeable medal haul because India did not add a gold, while countries above it continued to accumulate gold medals and increase their overall totals.China continued to dominate the Games after crossing the 200-medal mark, with 119 gold, 48 silver and 38 bronze for 205 medals. Japan and South Korea remained second and third.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleSeven medals, but no gold for IndiaIndia's seven medals on Sunday included two silver from squash and five from athletics.Parul Chaudhary produced one of the day's standout performances, breaking her personal best to win bronze in the women's 3000m steeplechase. She clocked 9:08.67, a new national record, to claim her second Asian Games steeplechase medal after winning silver at Hangzhou in 2023.Bahrain's Winfred Yavi won gold in 9:04.36, while Kazakhstan's Norah Jeruto Tanui took silver. India's Ankita finished fourth in a personal-best 9:19.24.Sarvesh Kushare and Ancy Sojan also won silver medals after leading their respective finals for significant periods. Sarvesh cleared 2.25m but finished second to Chinese Taipei's Chao Hsuan-Fu, while Ancy's 6.53m was bettered by China's Huang Yingying, who produced 6.55m with her final attempt.Harita Bhadra had earlier won bronze in the women's 200m in 23.20 seconds, edging Japan's Ido Abigeirufuka by 0.01 seconds.Tejaswin Shankar completed India's athletics haul with bronze in the decathlon. He won the final event, the 1500m, in 4:33.09 and finished with 7,934 points. Japan's Yuma Maruyama won gold with 8,123 points.Squash misses gold, boxing adds three assured medalsIndia's wait for a squash singles gold continued as both Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh lost their finals to Malaysian opponents. articles.title: Gleyber Torres' two-year run with Tigers comes to frustrating end
articles.summary: After making the All-Star team in 2025, persistent oblique issues this season kept free-agent-to-be Torres from playing up to his own high standards.
articles.body:
DETROIT — Gleyber Torres at least has kept his sense of humor through it all.

This has been a rough year for him, health-wise and otherwise, and that it has come in a contract year only compounds the disappointment.

His season and probably his Tigers' tenure, ended Tuesday, Sept. 22. He's not played since and he wasn't expected to play in the finale Sunday. And when he was asked his thoughts on his pending free agency, he gave a wry smile.

"I know my agent will have to work hard," he said. "I don't do too much this year. I do a little bit. Hopefully he does the job and gets me something good."

Torres will be going into his age-30 season. And after going through sports hernia surgery last winter , he's grinded through a season where he was put on the injured list twice with oblique strains.

"Unfortunately, this season has been awful," he said. "Twice injured. I don't feel like I performed like I am used to performing. Last year with the injury, this year with the injury, it never let me play like I can play. It sucks. I wanted to play really good coming off of last year when I helped the team a lot. This year, I didn't do much."

While he played a career-low 96 games and had a career-low 420 plate appearances (not counting the COVID season of 2020), he was still a 2-WAR player.

"I didn't feel as strong as I did last year," he said. "I tried to play a different way and I tried to push myself a little more, but I never felt good. For sure I kept playing because I have to play. But for myself, I never felt strong."

His slash-line wasn't far off his career norms — .260/.364/.363 with a .727 OPS — but, except for a few stretches, he wasn't as impactful has he was last season when he was the American League's starting second baseman in the All-Star game.

"I did all I could do to be healthy and help the team," he said. "It is what it is. Injuries suck, but they are part of the game. I will have the offseason to fix a couple of things and come back even stronger than ever and we'll see where I'm going to be next year."

He accepted the Tigers' qualifying offer last winter and earned $22.05 million this season. He understands that the odds of making more than that or getting a long-term contract this offseason, especially with the pending labor uncertainty, are long.

"I've had a lot of conversations with my agent," he said. "December is going to be different than it's been in the past but we don't know what it's going to be like. Injured twice, like, you know how the business is. We'll see. Hopefully I can get a deal I deserve."

He did not rule out the possibility of re-signing with the Tigers, but he sees the influx of young infielders coming up, like Hao-Yu Lee and Max Anderson, one of the few higher-level prospects who didn't debut this season.

"My time here was great," he said. "I like this group. I like the organization. I've enjoyed all of my teammates. It's a special group and I'm glad I got to play here. I will always be grateful for the opportunity here. Who knows about next year, but speaking in the present, it was good. The people here treated me like a brother from the beginning."

articles.title: Chiefs Announce Sudden Chamarri Conner Decision Hours Before Dolphins Game
articles.summary: The Chiefs announced a sudden Chamarri Conner decision just hours before their game against the Dolphins, putting the safety in focus. The post Chiefs Announ...
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs safety Chamarri Conner will not suit up Sunday in Miami , sidelined for a third straight week by the same knee that has trailed him through the first quarter of the 2026 season.

The Kansas City Chiefs safety went from doubtful to out with only about two hours to go before kickoff Sunday, leaving a secondary that has already logged two games without him to lean once more on a pair of backups against a Dolphins team still in search of its first win.

Conner was limited in practice all three days last week, according to the Chiefs' official injury report, before Kansas City tagged him doubtful Friday. Coach Andy Reid framed the workload as progress.

"He's making progress, so he's up practicing and moving around," Reid said Friday, as quoted by Arrowhead Pride , describing Conner's status heading into the weekend. The club made it official Sunday morning, ruling teh 26-year-old out for the Dolphins game. His next chance to return comes Oct. 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders .

Kansas City Chiefs' Chamarri Conner Injury Timeline

Conner has yet to play a snap in 2026. He sat out the opener against Denver and Week 2 against Indianapolis with the same knee, marking his third consecutive missed game to start the year. It is not his first extended absence. He also missed the final two weeks of 2024 with a concussion.

Born July 11, 2000, in Jacksonville, Florida, Conner starred at multiple positions in the secondary at Virginia Tech before Kansas City traded up with Minnesota to grab him in the fourth round, 119th overall, in the 2023 NFL Draft. He signed a four-year, $4.59 million rookie contract , according to Over The Cap, and has since collected a Super Bowl LVIII ring.

The safety's workload ballooned last season, when he played nearly every defensive snap and racked up a career-high 117 tackles. He has 230 tackles across three NFL seasons to go with four interceptions and three forced fumbles, one of which he returned for a touchdown against Cincinnati in 2024.

Safeties Jaden Hicks and Alohi Gilman have played every defensive snap through two games and will start again Sunday, with rookie Xavier Nwankpa in reserve. Hicks has already turned heads, posting 10 tackles in Kansas City's overtime win over Indianapolis, a workload that will only continue to grow as long as Conner remains sidelined.

Losing Conner costs the Chiefs their most versatile piece in the secondary, a safety who can play in the box, cover the slot and line up as a hybrid nickel. Without him, Kansas City may lean harder on cornerback Mansoor Delane to fill that role. Reid sounded confident Friday about Delane's availability.

"Good chance, yeah," Reid said, as quoted by Chiefs On SI , when asked if Delane would play against Miami.

Chris Jones and L'Jarius Sneed each carry no game-day designation despite limited practice work, and left tackle Josh Simmons is out for a third straight week with a training-camp back injury. The rest of Kansas City's roster, including quarterback Patrick Mahomes , is otherwise healthy.

Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's unit has already survived two full games without Conner, and Miami's offense has managed just 13 points per game so far. The real question hovering over Kansas City's secondary isn't whether it can cover for one missing piece. It's whether Hicks keeps holding up as an every-down starter rather than the rotational piece he was a year ago.

articles.title: Bills Get D.J. Moore Injury News Hours Before Chargers Game
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills get great injury news on $110 million WR before Week 3 game against Los Angeles Chargers. The post Bills Get D.J. Moore Injury News Hours Befor...
articles.body:
While most teams seem like battering rams for bad injury news, the unbeaten Buffalo Bills flipped the script on Sunday ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Los Angeles Chargers .

First, the Bills found out that wide receiver Keon Coleman would play after a week of doubt.

"Bills WR D.J. Moore , listed as questionable for today due to a shoulder injury, is expected to play vs. the Chargers, per source," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account.

" DJ Moore will be ACTIVE as I anticipated," Dr. Jesse Morse wrote on his official X account. "He's a DAWG, but will be at moderate risk of reinjury."

Moore had 5 receptions for 100 yards and 1 touchdown in a Week 1 win over the Houston Texans but was hurt early in a Week 2 win over the Detroit Lions .

Massive Praise for Moore After Opening Win

Sports Illustrated's Eva Geithem called Moore the NFL's "Top Offseason Addition" after his sparkling Week 1 debut.

"After they had struggled in recent matchups against the Texans, the Bills' offense was explosive against Houston on Sunday, racking up 36 points and 409 yards of offense," Geithem wrote on September 15. "One reason for the improvement? The addition of D.J. Moore. the Bills' prior lack of top-end receivers made it hard for them to challenge the Texans' defense, but with Moore—and tight end Dalton Kincaid being healthy—they were able to create big plays in the passing game and score 36 points. Case in point, Moore averaged 20 yards per catch as he hauled in five passes for 100 yards and a touchdown. The Bills had to pay a steep trade price to land Moore (a second-round pick for Moore and a fifth), but if he continues to have this positive of an impact on the passing game, it will be well worth the cost."

articles.title: Washington football plummets out of US LBM Coaches Poll
articles.summary: The Washington Huskies took a massive tumble down the US LBM Coaches Poll following a 27-24 loss to Minnesota.
articles.body:
Following a 27-24 loss to the Minnesota Golden Gophers, the Washington Huskies won't be sniffing the top 25 of the US LBM Coaches Poll for a while.

After beginning Big Ten play as the No. 23 team in the country, Jedd Fisch's team had a golden opportunity to move up the rankings and take advantage of some turmoil around the Big Ten, with three ranked teams in the conference losing. USC fell at home to Oregon, while Michigan suffered a last-second loss in the Big House to Iowa , and Wisconsin went on the road to take down Penn State.

However, Fisch's team looked largely unprepared to deal with coach P.J. Fleck's squad, as the Huskies went down 14-0 in the first quarter following an early interception from Demond Williams Jr. and another slow start from the offense. The end result? 20 points in the poll.

In a game full of self-inflicted blunders and mismanagement from the Huskies, one stood out above the rest. With UW down 27-17 with around 2:30 to play, wide receiver Chris Lawson picked up a first down and got out of bounds. That stopped the clock to move the chains, but the Huskies chose not to go up-tempo and instead made a late substitution, allowing Minnesota to do the same as the clock wound all the way down to the two-minute timeout, wasting a clock stoppage for Washington.

"I thought there was a point there that Chris got knocked out of bounds, and it was a first down. So then they were resetting the chains, so they stopped the clock on the first down. And then we wanted to get a touchdown," Fisch said after the game.

"We wanted to get a certain red zone play in. And we wound up subbing, and the sub came in way too late. And with that, then they got to hold another 10 seconds. So that's my fault. There was a certain personnel group that I wanted in the game for that play, so we wound up having to call it after the two-minute warning."

Now, the Huskies will have to head down to Los Angeles to face off with the No. 18 Trojans , who dropped six spots after their loss to the Ducks. Here's how the top 25 shaped up.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Jaguars live updates: Score, news, discussion from NFL Week 3
articles.summary: The Patriots are taking on the Jaguars in Week 3 of the NFL regular season.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are entering the third week of the 2026 NFL regular season trying to end a disappointing streak. They have started every one of their last five campaigns with a 1-2 record.

In order to prevent the same from happening and improve to 2-1 on the year for the first time since their Cam Newton-led 2020 campaign, the Patriots will need to beat another 1-1 squad on the road: the Jacksonville Jaguars , who won their season opener before dropping last Sunday's game in Denver .

The Patriots, meanwhile, are trending in an opposite direction based on an admittedly small two-game sample size: they lost the NFL opener before rebounding with a win over the Steelers one week ago. Can they make it two in a row? Let's find out together.

Welcome to our Patriots-Jaguars live tracker and community discussion.

Sunday, Sept. 27, 1 p.m. ET | EverBank Stadium (Jacksonville, FL) | Broadcast information | Inactives | Game day roster | Weather forecast

The Patriots won the toss and deferred, putting their defense on the field to start things off. A pair of Jacksonville penalties started them off moving backwards, before Trevor Lawrence 's attempt to pick up a 3rd-and-8 with his legs was stopped short.

New England 's offense started with two short gains by Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson to set up an opening 3rd-and-5. Forced to use a timeout to avoid a delay of game, Maye then connected with Mack Hollins for a 21-yard gain to move across midfield. The following third-down saw Maye's pass over the middle to Hunter Henry fall incomplete forcing a punt.

Jaguars' running back Bhaysul Tuten picked up their first first-down of the day getting around the left edge on the ground. New England's defense then buckled down, as a big third-down hit by Christian Gonzalez following a short completion led to a punt.

Maye found a pair of first downs with his legs and back to Mack Hollins to again move the offense across midfield. They're facing a 3rd-and-2, Stevenson just picked up enough on the ground to move the chains. As Maye then looked to push it downfield, the ball slipped out of his hand during his throwing motion which led to the Jaguars recovering the fumble.

An 18-yard completion to Parker Washington on third-down got the Jaguars offense on the move before the run game set them up just outside the red zone. Then inside the red zone, Lawrence found Josh Cameron over the middle for a 12-yard touchdown. | Patriots 0 : 7 Jaguars

Two short gains from TreVeyon Henderson set the Patriots up with a 3rd-and-3, where Maye looked to escape up the pocket and move the chains himself but was brought down for a 0-yard sack.

The Patriots defense generated a much needed turnover, as tight coverage from Jaylen Reed led to a deflected pass which Marcus Jones intercepted.

New England took over at the 21-yard line following the interception. Maye took off and found the end zone with his legs but the score was negated due to a holding call on Morgan Moses . The unit continued to go backwards as Romeo Doubs was called for offensive pass interference. A scramble drill double pass from Efton Chism III to Mack Hollins the short completion to Doubs set up a 3rd-and-7, where Maye extended and just missed a completion in the end zone to Hollins. Andy Borregales' 35-yard field goal was then good. | Patriots 3 : 7 Jaguars

After cutting into the Jaguars' lead on the previous drive, the home team fought back on its next possession. Methodically marching 65 yards in nine plays, the defense surrendered a 10-yard touchdown pass to ex-Patriot Jakobi Meyers . | Patriots 3 : 14 Jaguars

Drake Maye and company were in dire need of some momentum on their next drive, and they found it on the second play of the series when Drake Maye hit DeMario Douglas for a gain of 38. The pair nearly connected for another big gain two plays later, but Maye overshot the wideout for an incompletion on 2nd-and-10. Things did not get any better. A defensive holding penalty extended the series on a near-interception, and a Maye fumble on a scramble was recovered by the QB himself. However, he was not that lucky on a 3rd-and-goal from the 2-yard line: trying to hit Efton Chism, he was intercepted in the end zone by Travis Hunter .

articles.title: Leal y Guerrero ganan… y le mandan un recado al seleccionador de España
articles.standfirst: La joven dupla se llevó el FIP Platinum de Lyon y lo celebraron haciendo el gesto del teléfono por la no convocatoria al Mundial
articles.summary: La joven dupla se llevó el FIP Platinum de Lyon y lo celebraron haciendo el gesto del teléfono por la no convocatoria al Mundial
articles.body: Javi Leal y Fran Guerrero han sido las dos grandes ausencias de la lista de Juanjo Gutiérrez para el próximo Mundial de pádel que se celebrará en Doha a comienzos de noviembre. Pues la respuesta de estos dos jugadores no se ha hecho esperar, pues solamente tres días después de la noticia, han ganado un torneo y lo han celebrado con un mensaje al seleccionador que ya está dando la vuelta al mundo. Esta semana no había competición de Premier Padel, pero sí un FIP Platinum en Lyon, que es la categoría de torneo justo por debajo de los P2. Muchas de las mejores parejas del circuito, a excepción de las cuatro primeras, estaban inscritas, pero terminaron siendo Guerrero-Leal y Stupa-Sanz los que terminarían clasificándose a la final. El malagueño y el gaditano venían de ganar a Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo en el tercer set de las semifinales, habiendo tenido que sufrir también en cuartos de final. Mientras tanto, Stupa y Jon lo tuvieron más sencillo en la jornada del viernes, pero también tuvieron que sacar su billete a la final en el último momento. Un duelo muy igualado sobre el papel que no terminó defraudando. El ‘Papelito’ y el ‘DJ’ arrancaron algo mejor, más sólidos sobre la pista y anotándose por 6-4 la primera manga del encuentro. La reacción de Fran y Javi fue inmediata, igualando la contienda con otro 6-4 que lo mandaba todo a la tercera manga. Ahí, los andaluces fueron muy superiores, llevándose el título con un rotundo 6-1 que les acerca a los primeros puestos de la clasificación y que sigue evidenciando su gran momento de forma esta temporada. Nada más vencer, miraron a la cámara e hicieron el gesto del teléfono. Una señal muy evidente hacia Juanjo Gutiérrez, seleccionador español, que ha preferido llamar a Aimar Goñi y al propio Jon Sanz para completar la lista de ocho para representar a la ‘Roja’. “Hemos demostrado de lo que somos capaces”, dijo también Guerrero en la entrevista después del partido. Un mensaje claro tras una actuación memorable en tierras francesas. Para Franco y Jon supone un importante batacazo en sus aspiraciones. Desde que se juntaron no han tenido las mejores sensaciones e incluso han tenido varios tropiezos inesperados en Madrid y París. De hecho, perdieron su puesto como cuarta pareja en Roland Garros, por lo que este FIP Platinum se presentaba como una gran oportunidad para ellos. Si hubieran ganado, habrían adelantado nuevamente a Paquito Navarro y Martín Di Nenno, pero esta derrota hace que sigan estando como quintos en los sorteos, teniendo que verse las caras con algún cabeza de serie en cuartos de final. Están algo más cerca, pero sin recuperar ese importante privilegio. Próxima cita, el P2 de Rotterdam, donde volverán a tener una nueva oportunidad de demostrar todo su potencial.

articles.title: Pubs in Ireland refuse to screen Israel match in protest over Gaza genocide
articles.summary: Ireland has been thrust into the global spotlight over two controversial Nations League football games against Israel.
articles.body:
On match days, Peadar Browns pub in Dublin’s historic Liberties area is usually jam-packed with football fans piling in to watch the game on various screens.

As kickoff approached in the Republic of Ireland’s Nations League game against Israel on Sunday, there was a similarly busy crowd.

With one significant difference, though: none of the televisions were on.

The pub has made a deliberate decision not to show the game tonight in protest against Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza.

“We committed about a month ago not to show any of the upcoming Nations League fixtures until Ireland made a stand against Israel,” says owner Aidan Brown. “We didn’t show the Kosovo game, and we’ve absolutely no intention of showing the Israel games.”

Brown has been compiling a list of venues refusing to screen the match. At his last count, it included 140 pubs and bars in Ireland and abroad. He expected the number had risen before kickoff as tumultuous events within the Ireland team reverberated around the country.

Ireland, a staunch and long-standing ally of the Palestinian cause , has been thrust into the global spotlight over whether the team will play the two scheduled games against Israel.

Brown compares the atmosphere in Dublin to one of the most enduring sporting dramas in modern Irish history.

“I think this is just as big as Saipan and the Roy Keane saga in 2002,” he says.

Saipan became a national drama when Ireland captain Roy Keane left the 2002 World Cup squad in Japan after a confrontation with manager Mick McCarthy over training facilities.

This time the public debate across the island of Ireland is not about football standards, but moral ones.

In Derry, in the north of Ireland, Liam Doherty, another pub owner refusing to show the game, describes a similar sense of mobilisation.

“It has to come from the bottom up, and it has to come from a small nation,” says the owner of the Delacroix bar. “I think that we have to be the one that shows that this is just wrong.”

Rebecca O’Keeffe, chair of Irish Sport for Palestine, which has led the Stop the Game campaign, says the past week has shown just how far that mobilisation has spread.

“It’s a mass movement,” she says. “It’s reached corners of Ireland that maybe wouldn’t have been engaged with this issue before. It’s all people can talk about. We are past the point of symbolic gestures and hollow words.”

It’s not unanimous, but Irish public opinion is clearly against tonight’s fixture taking place.

A poll of Irish football supporters found 76 percent opposed to the match going ahead. Among athletes, 63 percent of members of the Professional Footballers’ Association of Ireland voted against playing the game.

But that groundswell of public sentiment has been ignored by those in charge of the sport in the country, the Football Association of Ireland (FAI).

In November, 93 percent of FAI members voted for the association to seek Israel’s suspension from UEFA competitions.

Yet when the FAI voted in July on whether the Republic of Ireland should play Israel, it chose to proceed with the fixtures. The motion passed 75 votes to 32 , with three abstentions. The FAI cited the consequences non-fulfillment could have for Irish football, such as potential points deductions.

Daniel Lambert, the Bohemian FC chief commercial officer who helped propose the original November motion, says the sequence explains much of the anger towards the FAI.

“It’s been mishandled from the very first day by the FAI,” he says. “The November vote was a very clear instruction from the membership, but they never really entertained not playing the games.”

Lambert argues that the FAI also failed to recognise what it could have gained by taking a stand.

“There are huge benefits to not playing,” he says. “Not only would it have the support of the Irish people … this would have enhanced the FAI’s reputation, not damaged it.”

Susan Shalabi, vice president of the Palestinian Football Association, believes the buck stops even higher up.

“The deeper issue is that the FAI and many others should never have been placed in this position,” she told Al Jazeera. “Had football’s international governing bodies [FIFA and UEFA] consistently applied their own rules, this dilemma would not exist.”

Instead, the decision has been left not with the governing bodies, but with the Irish players themselves.

Earlier this week, more than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter calling on the squad to boycott the fixtures. Team coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said some players were “really uncomfortable” playing, while midfielder Jason Knight said the games should not be happening.

Then, on Saturday, the fault line inside the squad became public.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu told his teammates he did not want to play. The players subsequently voted to fulfil the fixture, with reports suggesting eight had voted against playing. Bazunu was the only one who ultimately refused.

Lambert says Bazunu’s decision to stand alone was extraordinary.

“To do that on your own in a group of 25 players is staggering courage,” he says. “He’s represented Ireland more than those 24 players ever will. He has the respect of the Irish people forever.”

Amid the turmoil inside the Ireland camp, there have also been reports of players facing pressure from agents over the potential consequences of refusing to play, including concerns about their future careers.

Lambert, who is also the manager of hip-hop trio Kneecap , sees a parallel with what has happened in Irish music. When Irish-American rapper Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran’s US tour after speaking out for Palestine, the other supporting acts — including Irish artists Aaron Rowe and Beoga — subsequently withdrew in solidarity.

“We’ve seen a real watershed moment in music,” Lambert says. “I think this still has the potential to be one of those moments in sport.”

Next week, the Republic of Ireland has another Nations League game scheduled against Israel. Before then, they face Austria in Dublin, where the players will have to confront an angry home crowd. The pressure to boycott the second Israel game is only set to intensify.

Back at Peadar Browns, the televisions will stay off. Owner Aidan Brown sums up the sentiment of the country when he explains why.

“The points are just not important at all,” he says. “Football is just football. Sadly, it just doesn’t mean that much when a genocide is going on.”

articles.title: Dan Lanning blasts USC after Oregon's win, as Lincoln Riley officially enters hot seat in LA

articles.body: Week four of the college football season delivered yet again, with wild, last-second upsets in the Big Ten, season-changing wins for programs like Mississippi State and Florida, and high-profile matchups of big-name teams. Texas A&M-LSU reinforced that the Aggies were wildly overrated, Ole Miss' defense collapsed after the emotional, energetic win over the Tigers the prior weekend, and Iowa pulled off a miracle in yet another bizarre finish at Michigan Stadium. For USC, which brought in the number one recruiting class in the country, hired highly respected former TCU head coach Gary Patterson to run their defense, and brought back one of the top quarterbacks in the country in Jayden Maiava, it was more of the same under head coach Lincoln Riley. And Ducks' head coach Dan Lanning took the opportunity after the game to remind them of it. In his postgame news conference, Lanning praised the team's response after Moore's devastating, scary injury. He spoke about how prepared Raiola was for the moment, and said his decision-making was impressive after coming off the bench. He explained how his process has changed over time, which led to taking three points right before halftime instead of pushing for a touchdown. At the end of his remarks though, Lanning brought up his record against USC and what he believes it should mean for top LA area players. "Three wins against these guys," he said. "I guess if you're interested in winning football games and you're from this area, you should go to Oregon. If you want to go to a Chris Brown concert, you should go here." Ouch. And while there will be opportunities to turn the season around in coming weeks, there's little reason to expect it to. The result was a microcosm of Riley's tenure. articles.title: Netball World Cup: Northern Ireland qualifying 'surreal' - Caroline O'Hanlon
articles.summary: Northern Ireland netball vice-captain Caroline O'Hanlon says "not many outside of our camp expected us to qualify" after the booked their spot in the 2027 World Cup in Australia.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland netball vice-captain Caroline O'Hanlon said "not many outside of our camp expected us to qualify" after the side booked their spot for the 2027 World Cup in Australia.

Sheonah Forbes' side secured their place in Sydney after beating Wales and the Republic of Ireland during their impressive qualifying campaign in East Kilbride.

It will be the first World Cup for Northern Ireland since 2019, after they missed out on the 2023 edition in Cape Town.

"There wouldn't have been many outside of our camp who expected us to qualify," O'Hanlon told BBC Sport NI.

"It's so exciting, even since Friday, we've been inundated with well wishes and messages from home and people watching the games on BBC. It's been brilliant to have that exposure.

"It just seems surreal. We've been training away and we knew we had that potential, but obviously potential is one thing, getting it over the lines is a different thing and I am so proud of the group that we were able to get it over the line."

World-ranked number 15 Northern Ireland's emphatic 73-50 victory over Republic of Ireland in their final qualifier was not enough to secure one of the two qualification spots automatically.

However, Scotland's narrow win over Wales in Sunday's later game booked both teams spots with Wales, who are ranked ninth in the world, missing out.

"It was a real rollercoaster of a day," O'Hanlon continued.

"Obviously we started out with a hard-fought win against the Republic of Ireland, but we knew that we were still relying on Scotland.

"That match was just up and down the whole way through, so we were nerve-wrecked watching that. Just sitting in the stands, not being able to control anything, was nerve-wracking."

O'Hanlon was captain of the side when they finished 10th in the World Cup seven years ago.

But, now, the 42-year-old said the squad will head to Sydney with ambitions of competing for results rather than simply gaining experience.

"The last one we were at was in Liverpool and there was a lot of home support, but Sydney is the home of netball at the minute," O'Hanlon added.

"Sydney is the centre of the best league in the world. It'll be a brilliant spectacle and it's just class to be a part of it.

"The group will be going into the games not just to experience, not just to learn, but to actually go on and compete and try to win games and get results. That's the next step for us really."

articles.title: Luke Littler is facing 'unfair' treatment from sections of crowd, says former two-time world champion Adrian Lewis
articles.summary: Former two-time world champion Adrian Lewis has advice for Luke Littler on how to deal with hostile crowds; you can watch World Grand Prix Darts live on Sky Sports from September 28 - October 4
articles.body:
Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 ended in Amsterdam where the Briton complained about being repeatedly whistled at by Dutch supporters.

Littler even threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled by the vociferous crowd.

Lewis, a former two-time world champion, sympathised with teenage star Littler.

"It's very difficult. Obviously you're under a lot of pressure and certainly when he's going for everything, you put a lot more pressure on yourself as well," Lewis said.

"When you've got that going on I don't think it's nice, I don't think it's called for. At the end of the day, he's a young lad. He's one of the best players I've ever seen and I think it's unfair on him."

Lewis offered Littler advice. "It's difficult. What you're best off doing really is try not react to them," he said.

"If you just turn up there and just throw - engaging with the crowd because you've got to engage with them anyway because that's part of the job - but if they start booing and all that and whistling, just take no notice of them."

articles.title: Mr. Olympia 2026 Results, Prize Money Payouts for Winner and Top Contestants
articles.summary: For the fifth straight, year the Mr. Olympia Open division failed to crown a repeat champion. However, that didn't prevent Saturday's finals from being a thrilling affair, capped by Nick Walker's first-ever Open victory.
articles.body:
For the fifth straight, year the Mr. Olympia Open division failed to crown a repeat champion. However, that didn't prevent Saturday's finals from being a thrilling affair, capped by Nick Walker's first-ever Open victory.

Walker, who finished sixth at last year's Olympia Open and finished second at the 2026 Arnold Classic, beat out a tremendous field for his first Sandow Trophy.

It was obvious during Friday night's prejudging that defending Olympia champion Derek Lunsford, 2024 champ Samson Dauda, and 2026 Arnold winner Andrew Jacked were Walker's top competition.

Unsurprisingly, these four pushed one another during a drama-drenched Saturday evening full of exciting individual routines.

Dauda and Jacked both wowed with massive frames, while Lunsford appeared to be in the same championship form he brought a year earlier. However, Walker's combination of mass, symmetry, and a lean physique was enough to earn him the title of Mr. Olympia.

That's a title that came with a $600,000 prize purse, by the way.

While this year's Arnold Classic raised its first-place prize to $750,000, the Olympia kept the same prize structure as last year. However, that shouldn't (and doesn't) take away from the event's prestige.

The Arnold has become a premier bodybuilding event in its own right, but the Olympia is still the sport's most coveted prize.

Obviously, winning the Open was a massive goal for Walker, who changed his approach after failing to make the top five in 2025. He restructured his training routine and hired a new coach, Prabh Dhaliwal, in order to focus fully on training.

"I think overall, I just like being a robot," Walker said in a June YouTube video (h/t Doug Murray of Fitness Volt). "If I can find somebody that I know I can trust, I'll pick the robot. The process itself was extremely fun. I enjoyed doing it, learning my body, learning the ins and outs, going through the peaking process."

Walker's new approach paid off, as he managed to edge out Dauda and become the champion of the Olympia Weekend's biggest event. However, he was far from the only champion to to be crowned in Las Vegas this year.

The men's open is the highlight of Joe Weider's Fitness and Performance Weekend, but the following competitors emerged as champions as well:

Classic Physique: Niall Darwen ($100,000)

Fitness: Michelle Fredua-Mensah ($50,000)

Women's Physique: Natalia Abraham Coelho ($50,000)

Fit Model: Shealynn Burnett (Prize Not Announced)

Pro Wheelchair: Blake Colleton ($10,000)

articles.title: Ramos fires holders Portugal to 2-1 Nations League win in Norway
articles.summary: Goncalo Ramos starts in place of Cristiano Ronaldo and scores the winner for Portugal in Oslo.
articles.body:
Goncalo Ramos started in place of Cristiano Ronaldo and scored the winner, as Portugal made it back-to-back victories to start their UEFA Nations League title defence by beating Norway 2-1 in Oslo on Sunday.

Jorge Jesus’s men have responded well to their tame World Cup last-16 loss to Spain, having also beaten Wales 1-0 in Group A4 on Thursday.

The 41-year-old Ronaldo was named among the substitutes for the first time for Portugal since a Nations League game against Scotland in September 2024, and did not get onto the pitch as Jesus looks to manage his minutes across an expanded international break.

World Cup quarterfinalists Norway were left to rue some wasteful finishing in front of goal as they failed to build on their opening 3-2 win over Denmark.

The first big chance fell to Erling Haaland, but the Manchester City striker mishit his attempted volley after being picked out by Martin Odegaard, and Portugal goalkeeper Diogo Costa made the save.

The away team quickly made Haaland pay, as Joao Felix stroked a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the box in the 17th minute.

Haaland looked certain to equalise shortly afterwards when Costa spilled the ball into his path, but he was denied by a superb block from his City teammate Ruben Dias.

Costa foiled the Norway talisman again 10 minutes before half-time as the goalkeeper made an excellent stop from Haaland’s downward header.

Haaland finally converted six minutes into the second half, tapping in from Patrick Berg’s header across goal.

But Norway gave back the lead immediately, as goalkeeper Orjan Nyland passed the ball straight to Ramos, who coolly chipped it into the net.

Rafael Leao had a shot deflected onto the crossbar as Portugal pushed to make the game safe.

Nyland had his blushes spared when a VAR review ruled out another opportunistic Ramos effort for the tightest of offsides.

The goalkeeper waited for a long pass over the top to reach him, then took a swipe at thin air as Ramos got to the ball before him and rolled it into an empty net.

Norway threw everyone forward, including Nyland, in the closing stages, but could not find another leveller.

Ramos told Sport TV that it was an important win against a tough Norway side.

“It’s a great win on a difficult away trip. It’s been a great start [for new boss Jorge Jesus]. We’re working together and taking the manager’s ideas on board well,” he said.

“From here on, it’s all about improving and ironing out the kinks. We want to win every game. We’re always focused on victory in every match.”

images.caption: Portugal's Goncalo Ramos celebrates scoring at Ullevaal Stadion in Oslo, Norway [Paulo Novais/EPA]

articles.title: Americans rally in singles to win the Presidents Cup for the 11th straight time
articles.summary: US captain Brandt Snedeker won’t have to second-guess the outcome of this Presidents Cup. He went from blaming himself for a three-point deficit to watching the Americans deliver the biggest Sunday rout in tournament history to win for the 11th straight time.
articles.body: US captain Brandt Snedeker won’t have to second-guess the outcome of this Presidents Cup. He went from blaming himself for a three-point deficit to watching the Americans deliver the biggest Sunday rout in tournament history to win for the 11th straight time. Outplayed over three days in team matches at Medinah, the Americans flipped two key singles matches on the back nine — one from two-time major champion Collin Morikawa, the other from 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun. And it was a rush of red scores at the end. President Donald Trump was on the first tee for the start of 12 singles matches, and he kept his speech short. “It’s going to be a very interesting game of golf,” he said. That it was, even if the outcome was all to familiar. The Americans won nine of the 12 singles and halved the final match on the course when the Presidents Cup already was decided, adding to a 17-13 victory. Trump, the honorary chairman of the Presidents Cup, stuck around for the trophy presentation, just like he did after another American victory at Liberty National in 2017 during his first term. The U.S. rally wasn’t on edge the way it was in 2012 when Europe stormed from a 10-6 deficit at Medinah to win the Ryder Cup. The Americans at least had a home crowd on their side, loud and boisterous all day, and over the top on one occasion. Someone yelled in the backswing of Nico Echavarria, causing him to drop the driver as his ball sailed to the right. Scottie Scheffler barked at the fan, and after missing a birdie putt, he conceded a 30-foot par to the Colombian in a show of sportsmanship. Scheffler went on to win. So did Cameron Young and Justin Thomas and Chris Gotterup as the deficit shrunk and soon turned into another comfortable victory. “I told the guys last night that funny stuff happens here. Medinah has a history of funny things happening,” said Snedeker, who was on that losing Ryder Cup team in 2012. “Sure enough, they went out and played their (tails) off today. I’m so damn proud of those guys.” That group included Koivun, who just over a year ago was on the winning Walker Cup team for amateurs. Just four months ago, he helped Auburn to an NCAA golf title. And there he was Sunday, going from a 2-down deficit to a 2-up victory and hitting clutch shots on the 18th to secure a win. “The kid is special. He’s different,” Snedeker said. “You saw that for a 21-year-old kid to stand up there and hit those last two balls like he did. Not many people like that.” Patrick Cantlay had another moment, as he always seem to do in these events, holing a birdie putt from just inside 60 feet on the par-3 16th against hard-luck Adam Scott. Five matches remained on the course — the Americans were 1 up in three of them, the other two were all square. All the Internationals had to do was find three points from them. The Americans simply refused to budge. Koivun was 2 down through 10 holes to the Internationals’ top performer this week, Si Woo Kim, when he won three straight holes to flip the color to American red on the board. The kid drilled his tee shot on the 18th, and twirled his iron when he knew the approach was pure. He wound up with a 2-up victory, and then it was a matter of time. The clinching point came from Jacob Bridgeman, who was 1 down with three to play. He rolled in a 3-foot par putt for a 1-up victory over Min Woo Lee, assuring the Americans the 15 1/2 points they needed. “It was sort of on a knife’s edge all day,” Internationals captain Geoff Ogilvy said. “Some of those 1-downs that we had out there, if they’d flipped to 1-up, the numbers look really good, and who knows what momentum can give. “But look, it’s a very difficult thing to beat the U.S. in singles in the U.S,” he said. “They’re great players, and the crowd came out for them. They get a bit of red on the board, and the noise gets loud. They started the day with a lot to do and they all played great.” All the Internationals can do is regroup and try again at Kingston Heath in Australia is two years. Their only victory was at Royal Melbourne in 1998, and there was a tie in South Africa in 2003.

images.caption: Members of the USA team celebrate Jackson Koivun's win on the 18th green against the International team during a Presidents Cup golf tournament final round singles match at Medinah Country Club, Illinois, on Sunday, Sept. 27.
Jackson Koivun reacts to his birdie putt on the 12th hole on Sunday.

articles.title: Winners and Losers from a disappointing Seahawks loss to the Commanders
articles.summary: The Seahawks finally lost a game. It had to happen eventually, but to the Commanders?! That was unexpected.
articles.body:
Well, the Seattle Seahawks weren't going to win every game. They were also going to inevitably lose to a bad team, and to suggest Mike Macdonald would be immune to this would smack of arrogance. Almost every contending team, including teams coached by all-time greats over the years, manage to throw up a clunker at least once in a season. We accept this in every other sport but football.

With that said, I did not think they would lose this game to the Washington Commanders . It was a deceptive 33-31 shootout loss given how many short drives the Commanders scored, but it's still a loss that is about as disappointing as any I can recall in the Mike Macdonald era.

Alright, it's been a minute since we've had to do a negative Winners and Losers column. I gotta dust off the cobwebs for this one!

So much for JSN being done throwing passes. He is 1/1 for 14 yards on the season after the double pass to George Holani .

But the main thing he's paid for? He's still great at that. Another 10 catches for 128 yards and a couple of touchdowns. There were a couple of false starts and a drop by JSN, but he produces at such a comically high level that those negative moments are a blip on the radar. Of all the players he might be competing against for OPOY, it might be… Kenneth Walker ? Just saying.

The Seahawks got their non-JSN targets involved a lot more than in the previous two weeks. Horton had three grabs for 48 yards and Kupp had four for 46 and a touchdown. Seattle has to have a passing offense that does not live and die off of JSN's production, and while the Commanders pass defense is not very good, this was very welcome to see.

Brian Fleury unleashes A.J. Barner as a pass-catcher

Do the Seahawks have a screen game now? A.J. Barner had five catches for 69 yards and had his best game of the young season. Brian Fleury got his main tight end involved heavily and it worked out. Elijah Arroyo 's continued non-involvement is a tiny bit bothersome.

Sam Darnold 's pick 6 was costly, but he still played a great game

I cannot justify or defend the pick-six that Darnold threw. Bad read, bad decision, pretty much a back-breaker. But on a day when he's coming back from injury and had no run game to support him, he carried the load on offense. He finished 31/45 for 379 yards and four touchdowns, albeit with one more interception on a tip-drill. Darnold avoided pressure expertly and did not get sacked, making some excellent throws throughout the afternoon.

Even acknowledging the picks, his performance provided some relief in terms of his mobility and what the passing offense could look like for the rest of the season.

Welcome back to the end zone, Eric Saubert !

Saubert's previous end zone trip as a Seahawk was the most important two-point conversion in franchise history. His first actual touchdown as a Seahawk is, for now, a receiving touchdown. I do wonder if there is a stat correction coming if he did fumble before crossing the plane. It could be an "other" touchdown in the form of a rare offensive fumble recovery, but we'll see.

He had one of Seattle's two sacks, three tackles for losses, and three QB hits. Big Cat has not missed a beat entering 2026.

Jason Myers ' kicking struggles are behind him

Making a 57-yarder in wet conditions is big-time. He hasn't missed a kick yet this regular season.

Jadarian Price's ball security is a real concern

Two weeks in a row with a lost fumble. He didn't have a high volume of carries at Notre Dame but the ball security question marks were brought up back then. I have no issue with his benching; he's a rookie and you hope he gets better and learns some lessons. The cost is any sort of speed and elusiveness in Seattle's backfield. If he can't figure this out then he won't get a heavy workload any time soon.

The Rashid Shaheed contract is looking shaky

I've given it another week, there's still a lot of time left in the season, but Shaheed finished another game without a big return and he had just two catches for 14 yards. There's just not been enough out of him in this offense to start the year, and it looks more glaring when Tory Horton immediately outperformed him when he got extended snaps for the first time this season. At $17 million/year this is not the productivity Seattle should be getting. It makes you wonder if Horton having a healthy 2025 would've influenced the Shaheed decision.

The Seahawks had eight accepted penalties against them, including multiple pre-snap penalties on Jaxon Smith-Njigba and a false start on A.J. Barner. There are some real procedural problems that are hurting them on offense, and they've shown themselves to be undisciplined and a little disorganized in the early portion of this season.

The run blocking, as a whole, was abysmal

The Seahawks miss Anthony Bradford , perhaps? I don't know yet, because the Commanders run D has actually been good for two straight games and the Seahawks ran over the Arizona Cardinals last week without Bradford. But they are struggling in short-yardage in the low red zone, and are not resetting the line of scrimmage in their favor. I've said it for two straight weeks, but I am concerned about Abe Lucas' ability to anchor and move laterally. The worst runs seem to come on the right side of the field. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani didn't offer up anything more than Price on the ground, and Wilson's plodding style is more exposed when he can't immediately go north-south.

A grand total of 39 yards on 17 carries from the running backs. That ain't going to get it done.

A.J. Finley's first start will probably he his last

Tough ask to be thrust into the starting lineup after a mid-week calf injury for Julian Love . It's a nice reminder that not every preseason star translates into regular season action. Finley was picked on all game and was spared bigger plays against him thanks to an illegal formation penalty taking away a 48-yard touchdown run, as well as expedited review wiping out a long Dyami Brown catch. The penalty he got for roughness was complete junk, so I have to defend him there. But he was brutal and Seattle needs one of Love or Ty Okada back next week. Bare minimum, D'Anthony Bell should be elevated next week.

Derick Hall recorded a sack but wasn't noticeable in getting after Mariota . DeMarcus Lawrence at least had three QB hits, but it was otherwise a game in which neither Uchenna Nwosu nor Dante Fowler Jr made much of an impact. Leonard Williams was his usual excellent self, but Seattle needs more from its edges and not just the interior.

Michael Dickson might have had one of his worst games ever

Dickson had a touchback (his first of the season) on his first punt. His final three punts traveled 44, 38, and 40 yards while inside his own half of the field. It was a breezy day but he did nothing to flip the field, and that's part of why the Seahawks kept gifting the Commanders favorable field position.

For what it's worth, Seattle's kick coverage has not impressed throughout the season and seems to default give returners the ball at the 30 or better. That's why the defense was deceptively worse than it actually was (258 yards allowed, 3/13 on third down, four yards per play).

Seattle's special teams losses through free agency and injury are being felt here.

Josh Jobe did get picked on a bit and even beaten for a touchdown by Terry McLaurin but sometimes it's just better offense beating good defense. McLaurin is one of the best in the business and Jobe is going to have some days in which he loses some reps.

Devon Witherspoon looked like he was overpursuing on his angles a little too much, leaving him out of position on tackles. Wasn't his best game to me.

David Blough out-foxed Mike Macdonald on those last two third down plays. The blitz was beaten by Rachaad White running to the outside, while Mariota pulled on a keeper for the first time all game and secured the dagger.

I'm oddly not too worried about this loss. It's a bad one, but it took a lot for Seattle to still lose by two points on the road. If they drop the Los Angeles Chargers game next week? Then it's time to worry about this squad. articles.title: Kyle Larson Dominates Kansas and Wins Hollywood Casino 400!
articles.summary: Kyle Larson put together a dominant performance Sunday at Kansas Speedway, winning the Hollywood Casino 400 and picking up his second victory of the 2026 NAS...
articles.body:
Kyle Larson put together a dominant performance Sunday at Kansas Speedway, winning the Hollywood Casino 400 and picking up his second victory of the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Chase.

Larson led 235 of the 267 laps and controlled much of the afternoon before battling Chase Briscoe for the win in the closing stages. Larson eventually passed Briscoe with six laps remaining and held on to take the checkered flag.

Larson came out strong from the start, winning both Stage 1 and Stage 2.

The No. 5 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet led 78 of the first 80 laps and continued to control the race through the second stage. Austin Cindric and Denny Hamlin remained near the front for much of the afternoon, but Larson consistently found his way back to the lead.

Larson's afternoon became even more impressive as the race continued. He repeatedly managed restarts and pit stops while keeping himself in position for another Chase victory.

The race finally became a battle in the closing stages.

Chase Briscoe stayed close to Larson after the final round of green-flag pit stops. With 30 laps remaining, Briscoe made his move and passed Larson for the lead.

For the first time all afternoon, Larson found himself chasing another car for the top spot.

Briscoe held the lead for several laps, but Larson refused to let him get away. With 11 laps remaining, Larson closed back in and began applying pressure.

Both drivers made contact with the outside wall while fighting for the lead.

Then, with six laps remaining, Larson made his move.

He passed Briscoe and retook the lead, setting himself up for the final run to the finish.

Once Larson got back out front, there was no stopping him.

He crossed the finish line 0.565 seconds ahead of Austin Cindric to secure the victory. Denny Hamlin finished third, Briscoe recovered to finish fourth, and Ryan Blaney completed the top five.

The win is Larson's fourth career victory at Kansas Speedway and his second win in the first four races of the 2026 Chase.

Larson also earned a perfect 76-point day, leading the most laps, winning both stages and taking the race victory.

Larson's victory continues his strong postseason run and gives him another major boost in the championship battle.

Behind him, Cindric, Hamlin, Briscoe and Blaney rounded out the top five, while several other Chase drivers finished inside the top 10.

Kansas delivered another important race in the Chase, but once again, Larson was the driver standing in Victory Lane.

The NASCAR Cup Series now moves on to the next stop in the 2026 Chase as the championship battle continues.

articles.title: Kyle Larson Adds to NASCAR Cup Points Lead With Dominant Kansas Win

Larson put on a clinic as his 235 laps led broke his own record of most circuits led at Kansas. The defending Cup Series champion also surpassed Bill Elliott for 19th place on most laps led all-time in Cup Series history.

With the dominant performance, "Yung Money" extended his points lead from one over Denny Hamlin to 26. Hamlin maintained a reasonable gap between himself and the Hendrick Motorsports star, finishing third and totaling 17 stage points.

Christopher Bell moved into third place in the standings, passing Joey Logano, after notching 12 stage points and finishing sixth. However, the dominant Larson win caused Bell to lose ground on the points lead as he is now 50 points behind.

Logano, who entered 16 points behind Larson, is now 67 points out of the top spot after a 20th-place finish at Kansas.

Tyler Reddick failed to score any stage points on Sunday and wound up finishing 11th. Despite having a series-high five wins in 2026, Reddick finds himself seventh in the standings, 111 points behind Larson.

Carson Hocevar took a hit in the championship standings as a 33rd-place result sent the driver of the No. 77 from eighth to 11th in the rankings. Chase Elliott slipped from 12th to 13th place in the standings despite recording an eighth-place finish.

articles.title: Astros win AL West with 81-81 record, worst for first-place team, beat A's 9-0
articles.summary: The Houston Astros won their fifth AL West title in six years despite finishing with the worst record for a first-place team, beating the Athletics 9-0 Sunda...
articles.body:
WEST SACRAMENTO, Calif. (AP) — The Houston Astros won their fifth AL West title in six years despite finishing with the worst record for a first-place team, beating the Athletics 9-0 Sunday behind Lucas Spence's two-run triple to finish at 81-81.

Nick Allen had just doubled leading off the eighth with the Astros leading by eight runs when Texas lost at Minnesota , assuring the Astros of their ninth postseason trip in 10 years after missing out in 2025.

Houston will host the Chicago White Sox in a best-of-three Wild Card Series starting Tuesday. The Astros finished one game ahead of Texas (80-82) but would have earned the division title even with a defeat because they held the tiebreaker.

Houston had the lowest winning percentage for a team reaching the postseason in a non-shortened year, breaking the mark set when the 2005 San Diego Padres went 82-20.

Yordan Alvarez finished as the major league batting leader at .316, going 1 for 4.

The Athletics went 64-98 in their second season at a Triple-A ballpark in West Sacramento before a planned move to Las Vegas in 2028, down from 76-86 last year. They drew 10,022 for their season finale at Sutter Health Park and finished with a major league-low 799,240 home attendance, the only team not to reach 1 million.

Jose Altuve 's RBI groundout, Yainer Diaz 's run-scoring double and Spence's two-run triple built a 4-0 lead in the third against Brady Basso (1-4), who allowed four runs and three hits in one inning.

Christian Walker 's solo home run and Yordan Alvarez's RBI single extended their lead to 6-0 in the sixth inning.

Ethan Pecko (3-0) allowed one hit in three innings.

Houston has not announced its probable pitcher for Tuesday.

articles.title: 2026 Walmart NW Arkansas Championship: Yuna Nishimura cruises to first LPGA victory
articles.summary: Yuna Nishimura played a flawless back nine after allowing the chasing pack to get close early and won the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship by five shots for...
articles.body:
ROGERS, Ark. — Yuna Nishimura played a flawless back nine after allowing the chasing pack to get close early and won the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship by five shots on Sunday for her first LPGA victory.

A six-time winner on the Japan LPGA, the 26-year-old Nishimura closed with a 5-under 66 for a three-day total of 21-under 192 at Pinnacle Country Club.

"I still can't believe it. I still shake my hand. But, yeah, I'm proud of myself and, yeah, I'm super happy," Nishimura said.

Leading by five shots entering the day after back-to-back 63s, Nishimura shot even-par 36 on the front nine while another Japanese player, Aki Iwai, made a charge with six birdies in seven holes to start the back nine.

Iwai shot a bogey-free 62 and tied for second with Chanettee Wannasaen (65) and In Gee Chun (67).

"This week greens are so soft," Iwai said. "Especially today. So I was like -- I need more aggressive. Like, yeah, I need hit three, four yards past the pin usually."

Nishimura opened a three-shot lead over Iwai with an eagle on the par-5 14th hole after she reached the green with a fairway wood over water . She added two more birdies to shoot 5-under 30 on the back nine.

"I told myself to go aggressive until the very end and I went for it," she said.

Lauren Coughlin, who set an LPGA record by opening with nine straight birdies to shoot a career-best 61 on Saturday, closed with a 66 and finished in a tie for 12th, eight shots back.

Lottie Woad, the seventh-ranked player in the world who helped Europe to victory over the U.S. in the Solheim Cup two weeks ago in the Netherlands, withdrew with an illness. The English player was six shots off the lead through two rounds.

Two players made holes-in-one Sunday. Yealimi Noh aced the par-3 15th hole with a 9-iron from 136 yards, the first of her career. Mao Saigo holed a 7-iron from 159 yards on the par-3 third, also her first ace.

articles.title: Lakers GM addresses LeBron leaving for Philadelphia
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers general manager talked about LeBron James' departure for Philadelphia during Lakers media day on Thursday.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka publicly addressed LeBron James ' departure in free agency over the summer.

James, 41, played the last eight seasons with the Lakers before he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. He led the Lakers to six playoff appearances, including winning the NBA Finals in 2020 and an appearance in the Western Conference Finals in 2023.

"I thought it would be appropriate at the front to express gratitude for the LeBron era here," Pelinka said at Lakers preseason media day on Thursday. "Clearly, new team and new players, and that's what we're going to talk about today. But we as an organization are still grateful for the run that we had with him here.

"The Lakers have become – as they should – a perennial playoff team. Won a championship, went to the Western Conference finals. It was a great era, and we're grateful for it. I think it's important to say that at the onset as we turn into a new chapter."

Following James' departure, the Lakers revamped their roster with a number of signings and trades to build a supporting cast around star Luka Dončić .

LA's offseason included re-signing Austin Reaves to a long-term deal, trading for Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz and acquiring veterans Kevon Looney and Collin Sexton .

"Once we got the news from LeBron and Rich that he was going to choose a different organization, we built a thesis for what we wanted this team to be heading into this season, (head coach) JJ ( Redick ) and I together," Pelinka said.

"There were three fundamental pillars of what we wanted to accomplish in the offseason. … Re-signing Austin (Reaves), putting together a trade to acquire Walker Kessler, and then building out our team with young players that could dribble-pass-shoot, and have brought the average age of our roster to around 26 or 27, which lines up so perfectly with building a team around Luka Dončić."

Pelinka made it clear that the Lakers are forward-looking and expressed optimism over the team's future. He also said there were no hard feelings between the Lakers organization and James following his departure.

"Again, we're grateful for the LeBron era. I think the communications with him this offseason were held diplomatically, professionally and honestly," Pelinka said. "I'm so thankful for the partnership that we had that continued up until this summer when a decision was made for him to play for another team. It was done amicably, professionally, gracefully. We looked at the whole thing with gratitude, because it's been an incredible era for us here."

articles.summary: Another game, another wild 49ers injury, this time to Mike Evans.

The San Francisco 49ers suffer more weird injuries than just about any team in the NFL. New addition Mike Evans went down during the team's Week 3 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals , and it's another injury that seems pretty confusing on first blush. It happened shortly after Evans executed a perfect hook-and-ladder with teammate Deebo Samuel for an 80-yard touchdown .

Evans ran a route in the third quarter and came up lame. He was sandwiched by two Cardinals defenders on the previous play but stayed in the game. Evans was evaluated on the field, and eventually carted to the locker room. Watch the play here.

Evans needed help just to get off the field. It sure feels like he reaggravated something from the previous play, but it still seems pretty weird that he stayed in the game and didn't show the effects of the injury until his next route.

Here's Evans being helped off the field and carted to the locker room.

There's speculation that Evans may have injured his ribs . Hopefully it's not a vital organ injury.

We'll update this post when Evans' injury status is announced.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland 'raised awareness worldwide' in Israel game
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson says his players "raised awareness worldwide" after they chose not to engage in pre-match formalities with...
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said his players "raised awareness worldwide" after they chose not to engage in pre-match formalities with Israel.

The Republic of Ireland and Israel players did not shake hands and the Irish squad bowed their heads when Israel's anthem was played before their 3-0 Uefa Nations League win in Hungary .

There was also no exchange of pennants between Republic of Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel skipper Manor Solomon , who did not shake hands.

The fixtures, being played at neutral venues, have been embroiled in controversy since February when the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

The Republic of Ireland players have faced calls to withdraw from the games because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war with a "Stop The Game" campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - gathering pace.

"It has been so difficult for so many players," Hallgrimsson told broadcaster RTE after the game.

"I hope that will not be in the next game because they have shown support to the protest, they have raised awareness worldwide, not only in Ireland, on the subject and that is normally the reason for protesting, to raise awareness of a situation.

"I think these players have done that with all their actions, with all that they have been saying. No more than Gavin Bazunu , but the others have done it here on the pitch and how they have shown their actions, so I hope people understand that."

The Republic of Ireland players voted to fulfil the fixture during a lengthy meeting at the team's hotel in Debrecen on Saturday.

Later on Saturday, goalkeeper Bazunu confirmed he had withdrawn from the squad, saying he felt it "would be wrong to participate" in Sunday's game and the return fixture in the Serbian town of Backa Topola on 4 October.

The Irish players wore black armbands, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said on Saturday was a gesture "in recognition of all lives lost in the [Gaza] conflict".

After scoring the Republic of Ireland's third goal, Jack Moylan removed his armband and kissed it before kissing his team's badge.

The Republic of Ireland players were jeered by the small number of Israel fans in attendance when they emerged for their pre-game warm-up.

While the FAI confirmed no tickets would be sold to Republic of Ireland supporters, a handful of fans were spotted inside the stadium.

Hallgrimsson confirmed Bazunu would be included in the squad for Thursday's game against Austria in Dublin, but not for the second match against Israel.

"I think he is very happy that we have won the game," said Hallgrimsson.

"Nobody was questioning his decision. It was only the timing that was difficult for us to kind of react to it, but none of us were asking him not to take his stand and now he's flying back with us on the plane."

When asked if player's opinions regarding the fixture were taken into account when selecting his team for Sunday's game, Hallgrimsson said: "Absolutely not.

"This team selection was about who we thought could make the best performance for Ireland."

During a dramatic day on Saturday, doubts emerged over whether the game would take place after the Republic of Ireland's pre-match news conference was postponed because of the squad meeting.

When the news conference commenced at 14:30 BST on Saturday - more than five hours later than planned - Courell said a players' vote on whether to play the game passed by a "significant majority".

Courell added that the Republic of Ireland would not engage in pre-match formalities such as handshakes.

In 2024, the Ireland women's basketball team chose not to shake hands with Israel players or stand on court for the anthems before a EuroBasket qualifier in Riga, but the teams did exchange handshakes when they met again last year.

The Republic of Ireland have faced calls to boycott the matches since the Nations League draw in February.

Last November, the FAI approved a motion calling for Uefa to suspend Israel from Uefa competitions.

In May, the team's friendly against Qatar was interrupted after fans threw tennis balls featuring the Palestinian flag on to the pitch .

In June, the FAI confirmed their home fixture would be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola instead of Dublin's Aviva Stadium, citing "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil".

At an extraordinary general meeting in July, delegates backed an FAI motion to proceed with the games amid concerns that boycotting the fixtures would cause "significant and lasting harm" for the association.

Calls for the Republic of Ireland to boycott the games have intensified in recent weeks. Earlier this week, more than 160 Irish athletes signed an open letter by Irish Sport for Palestine group urging the team not to play.

Courell also said last week Uefa had rejected a request for the Republic of Ireland and Israel to be kept apart in future competition draws.

Tensions between the teams were raised this week when the Israel Football Association accused Hallgrimsson of "ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity" after the coach said, "we're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide".

Speaking on Saturday, Hallgrimsson said it was "a wrong word for me to use", while Israel FA head of communications Shlomi Barzel said he would not apologise for his association's response but said he would "take back the word stupidity".

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

Israel has repeatedly denied that it has committed genocide, as well as war crimes and crimes against humanity. It says its military operations in Gaza have been conducted in self-defence and in accordance with international law.

articles.title: Takeaways as Lions top Jets to collect second win in 2026
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions improved to 2-1 with a 31-24 win over the New York Jets. What are some of the key takeaways?
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions are 2-1. Detroit hung on to down the New York Jets (1-2) from Ford Field, 31-24.

It was another thriller from Ford Field. Detroit built a two-touchdown lead after Jahmyr Gibbs ' second touchdown early in the fourth quarter.

But, like its season opener against the New Orleans Saints , the Lions watched a big lead slip away. Similar to that Week 1 victory, the Lions found a way late in a stressful finish at home.

The Lions' offensive line deserves credit for a better outing up front in the run game. A week after the Buffalo Bills ' defense limited Detroit to just 66 rushing yards and Jahmyr Gibbs to only 52, Gibbs and the Lions' running game bounced back.

Detroit outrushed New York, 131-58, and that wound up being one of the big keys in the game.

Gibbs just does some incredible things out there individually, though. The 5-foot-9, 202-pound running back's greatness was on display during his 17-yard touchdown run where he threw on the brakes and then reversed field after making multiple Jets defenders miss en route to the end zone.

Gibbs is an all-timer and that's clear every time he laces them up. The Alabama product climbed in the franchise's record books with his three-touchdown day.

Geno Smith lights up Lions' defense for 321 passing yards

Geno Smith made some pretty amazing throws on Sunday and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq and star receiver Garrett Wilson combined for multiple spectacular grabs.

So, to some degree, tip your cap to Smith and Co. on Sunday. But, after Tyler Shough threw for more than 400 yards in the opener, Josh Allen did what he wanted to do in Week 2 and Smith finished 31 of 37 passing for 321 yards with three touchdowns, it's obvious that Detroit's kryptonite is exactly what many suspected it would be.

The secondary and pass coverage is a major, major issue for Detroit's defense. If Detroit wants to truly contend for a Super Bowl, Lions general manager Brad Holmes has to make an in-season move to bolster this defense.

The Lions' defense got to Smith five times, including Chuck Clark on the game-sealer. Clark went untouched on a blitz to Smith, knocked the football loose and Jack Campbell scooped it to secure the 31-24 win.

DJ Wonnum had a two-sack day, Alim McNeill had a sack, and Aidan Hutchinson and Skyler Gill-Howard had a half-sack.

It's been a great start to the season from Jared Goff. Just another business-like, efficient day in the office for Goff.

The 31-year-old completed 25 of 32 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns. Goff has now completed 70.6% of his passes for 802 yards with eight touchdowns and no interceptions.

Goff spread the football around to eight different pass-catchers.

It was good to see Isaac TeSlaa make multiple key plays in this game. TeSlaa reeled in a 5-yard pass from Goff on a 4th-and-2 snap that set up Amon-Ra St. Brown 's 4-yard touchdown grab a few plays later.

Then, in the Lions' game-winning drive, TeSlaa jumpstarted the drive with a 49-yard reception.

TeSlaa finished with three catches for a team-leading 66 yards.

Sione Vaki had the most touches of his career on Sunday. With Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve and expected to be sidelined until December, the Lions need other running backs to help lessen the load a bit on Gibbs.

Vaki was able to do that on Sunday, carrying six times for 26 yards and catching a pass for 11 yards.
