articles.title: Pirates GM Ben Cherington Comments on Brandon Lowe's 2026 Impact, Free Agency
articles.summary: Pirates GM Ben Cherington praised Brandon Lowe's impact on and off the field as the veteran heads into free agency after a standout 2026 season.
articles.body:
Brandon Lowe gave the Pittsburgh Pirates exactly what they hoped for when they acquired him. Now, the second baseman has given the team a decision to make.

Lowe put together one of the best offensive seasons of his career in 2026, batting .260 with 35 home runs, 96 RBIs, 94 runs scored and an .824 OPS across 150 games. His 35 home runs led the Pirates.

Lowe is now headed for free agency, and Pirates general manager Ben Cherington made it clear that Pittsburgh would like to find a way to keep him.

"It's gone remarkably well on and off the field," Cherington said to Aiden Stepansky . "I mean, he's been everything we could have hoped for as a player and also in the clubhouse, and we know how his teammates feel about him. They express that, it's good."

Lowe has left the door open to returning to Pittsburgh while also preparing to test his value on the free-agent market, according to Dominic Campbell of Pittsburgh Pirates on SI .

"It's been incredible," Lowe said. "I've loved my time here. Thank everybody from the staff to players to the fans that are coming out and watching. They made this home. They feel like home. They supported us like we've been here for a long time."

Lowe added that he has enjoyed his time with the Pirates and would be grateful for his experience in Pittsburgh regardless of what happens this offseason.

"If this is it, we're deeply grateful for everybody in this organization," Lowe said. "Who knows, there's always an opportunity I get to deal with you guys' questions next year. It's not the greatest of answers, but it's a bridge we'll cross when we get there. We'll see what happens."

Cherington similarly left the door open, saying the Pirates will have more conversations with Lowe in October while evaluating their options for the offseason.

"We'll have some things to talk about and plenty of time in October to have more conversation with him about that," Cherington said. "We just need to learn more about what opportunities are out there for us, and he's put himself in a strong position too."

The 32-year-old also made an impact beyond the batter's box, earning praise from Cherington and his teammates for his presence in the clubhouse.

"Would be a great outcome if he's a Pirate and think the world of him and the job he's done," Cherington said.

articles.title: Brandt Snedeker makes comment about Donald Trump and Jackson Koivun after the USA win the Presidents Cup
articles.summary: Brandt Snedeker captained the United States Presidents Cup team to victory at Medinah in the end. It’s fair to say that the US won the Presidents Cup in spit...
articles.body:
Brandt Snedeker captained the United States Presidents Cup team to victory at Medinah in the end.

It's fair to say that the US won the Presidents Cup in spite of Snedeker, not because of him, as harsh as that may sound.

After his team won the singles by a scoreline of 9.5–2.5, the US captain made some interesting comments about Donald Trump and Jackson Koivun.

Donald Trump made a speech on the first tee ahead of the Sunday singles at Medinah in an attempt to inspire the US Presidents Cup team.

Jackson Koivun was one of the standout performers for the Americans, winning a vital point against the Internationals' star man.

And Snedeker praised the influences of both Trump and Koivun after the United States romped to victory on Sunday at Medinah.

Brandt Snedeker comments on Donald Trump after USA win the Presidents Cup

Snedeker spoke to reporters after his team got the job done on Sunday, and he responded when asked how he felt about the win over the Internationals.

" Yeah, pretty good. You asked me some pretty tough questions this morning, " he said.

" I think these guys never lost faith. I know what that team room is like. I told the guys last night that funny stuff happens here. Medinah has a history of funny things happening. Sure enough, they went out and played their a–––– off today. I'm so proud of those guys.

" I cannot get over what Jackson Koivun did today. I put him in a really tough spot out there. We thought he could handle it. Sure enough, he did. He went out there and looked like the stud we know he's going to be. So proud of Jacob Bridgeman getting his first point as a Presidents Cup rookie.

" All these guys fought for each other, fought for this country, fought for this team. And one last shout out to Donald Trump, President Trump. He told me I was going to bring some energy today for you guys, you guys need it, and I told him if we did this, he gets all the credit. Thank you, President Trump. "

Brandt Snedeker praises Jackson Koivun after USA's Presidents Cup win

Snedeker was also asked about Koivun's performance on Sunday at Medinah.

" The kid is special. He's different, " the 46-year-old replied.

" You saw that for a 21-year-old kid to stand up there and hit those last two balls like he did, not many people like that. I've got a team full of them over there but they're very rare to find.

" He's a great kid, got a great family. I got to meet his parents this weekend, and they've done a great job raising that young man. I'm so proud of him. "

Koivun showed up when it mattered during the Sunday singles at the Presidents Cup.

And him turning around his match against Si Woo Kim played a huge role in the Americans' getting the better of the Internationals.

articles.title: Padres close strong, shift their focus to Game 1 vs. Cubs on Tuesday
articles.summary: The Sporting Tribune's Fernando Ramirez writes that now that the regular season is over the San Diego Padres focus is on making some postseason magic.
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO, Calif. -- The San Diego Padres played their 162nd game of the 2026 MLB season on Sunday, finishing with a 9-4 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks .

They ended the regular season with a 91-71 record, clinching their third consecutive 90-win season.

After Sunday's victory, there will be roster questions to answer, especially when it comes to starter Randy Vásquez, who delivered six innings of one-run baseball on 68 pitches while allowing only three hits.

"Great outing by Randy today," Padres manager Craig Stammen said. "As far as Randy being available for the wild card series, we'll talk about that after today's game and decide if he'll be on the roster or if we want to save him for the the NLDS. If we get there."

The game between the Padres and Diamondbacks got interesting after the home team jumped out to a 4-1 lead thanks to a Manny Machado RBI single, a Gavin Sheets home run, a Ty France RBI single and a Freddy Fermin RBI double from the third through sixth innings.

Then Griffin Canning entered the game and unraveled, allowing five hits and three runs on 35 pitches. Obviously, Stammen wasn't going to use a playoff arm to get through the final game of the regular season.

Soon, it was a 4-4 game heading into the bottom of the seventh.

The Padres loaded the bases before Jake Cronenworth drew a walk to give them a 5-4 lead. Fermin followed with a single to left that scored two more runs, extending the lead to 7-4.

Teams always talk about "rock bottom" and how that moment tested them. For these San Diego Padres, it came on July 1, when the same Chicago Cubs they will face Tuesday in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series thrashed them 23-3 at Wrigley Field.

Chicago hit eight home runs, tying a Cubs franchise record, while Walker Buehler allowed a career-high nine runs.

San Diego was 43-42 and in ninth place in the NL standings at the time. After that game, the Padres lost three of four to the Los Angeles Dodgers and looked like a team with no direction.

Since that point in the season, the Padres are 42-22 (.656), tied with Milwaukee for the best record in MLB over that span.

"I think these guys have found out that they can handle about anything and still come out on top," Stammen said. "I think that's a good lesson to be learned, and builds resiliency and toughness, and those are good trades to have in the postseason."

Their offense has turned things around and become more efficient, with players like Dustin Harris seemingly coming out of nowhere to become their No. 2 hitter.

Lately, they have been on a remarkable run, winning 14 of their last 15 games while 20-year-old rookie Ethan Salas has emerged as their top option at catcher.

Last year, the Padres limped into Chicago for the playoffs, losing Game 1 before bouncing back to win Game 2. Game 3 was a disaster, with some of manager Mike Shildt's decisions coming under scrutiny in a 3-1 loss that ended their season.

"That was last year," Fernando Tatis Jr. said. "I don't really go back to that, but seriously brand new opportunity. Like I said, we better take advantage of that."

It won't be easy. The Padres went 1-5 against the Cubs this season and were even swept by Chicago at Petco Park.

But those were the Padres who struggled earlier in the season, not the red-hot team that has emerged over the last few weeks.

"It's a good matchup," Cronenworth said. "It's a great team. You know it'll be fun. I think no matter who you're playing in the playoffs, you gotta bring your A game, no matter where it is. Obviously, it'll be fun to play here at home."

One advantage the players know they will have is Petco Park. They have seen how loud Padres fans can get during the postseason.

"It's home," Machado said. "I mean these guys bring it every single year, so come home and play how we always play in front of them. It's always great."

Buehler was asked about the difference between earning a bye in the Wild Card round and having to keep playing immediately after the regular season.

"I think there's benefits to both," Buehler said. "I think when you're playing well, you want to keep playing, and we're playing well. So I think you know this benefits us."

He has experience with the extra rest after spending years with the Dodgers, who experienced both the benefits and drawbacks of having time off before beginning their postseason run.

Their postseason begins Tuesday at 7 p.m. PT, when they will have an opportunity to prove that the team everyone has watched over the final stretch of the regular season is the real San Diego Padres. Michael King will get the start in Game 1.

"Being able to piece that all together in September, when it really, really matters, and when you're going for something," Sheets said. "Not only clinch a spot in the playoffs, but to work around and get home for an advantage. Credit to credit to this clubhouse because that was that was an incredible run."

articles.title: Giants show how they can survive without Jaxson Dart in win over Titans
articles.summary: The Giants found a winning formula without Jaxson Dart in grinding out a 12-7 victory against the Titans.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- It's not going to look pretty. Not anymore.

Remember 2022? Picture that. All over again. Only with more competence and less reliance on the horseshoe the Giants stashed under their bench that season.

Jaxson Dart is gone. Maybe he'll be back for the playoffs, but unlikely. For New York to win without him, it must drag its opponents to the deep end and see if they can swim.

That's what the Giants did with the Titans. And with the game on the line, Cam Ward drowned. His egregious end-zone interception, which Jevon Holland gleefully snatched from the air, sealed New York's 12-7 win .

If the Giants are to survive the post-Dart era, this is the recipe to do so.

"They're never perfect," said John Harbaugh . "They need to be us doing what we need to do to win games."

The Titans are not good. Robert Saleh has his hands full in Year 1, and old friend Brian Daboll is doing very little to endear himself to those in Nashville, Tenn.

It took the Titans until the final possession of the first half to get their first first down. They didn't reach the red zone until the penultimate possession of the game. They had just 81 yards on the ground, averaging 3.9 per carry.

Then there was Ward. He missed throws high and missed them low. If he looked left, he missed someone open right. If he looked right, he missed the guy left.

This game is not close if the Giants have their quarterback.

The Titans began Sunday with five straight three-and-outs. New York's second-year quarterback, who was close to perfect in the season opener against the Cowboys, buries them if spotted that many opportunities.

But that's no longer the reality the Giants live in. It's all about ending with more points than your opposition, and leaving the style points to others.

"Let me ask you something," said Jameis Winston . "Would the old New York Football Giants have won (this) game? They said no. So it's good when you're able to find way to have one of those days."

Winston rebounded slightly from Monday night's disaster in L.A. He completed 14 of 22 passes (63.6 percent) for 118 yards. He didn't turn it over.

The Giants ran for 138 yards on the ground, led by Cam Skattebo (60) and Najee Harris (52). They moved the ball -- three times getting to the Tennessee 21 or close -- all possessions ending with Dominic Zvada field goals.

It was enough. Barely. Because the Titans finally broke through, going 91 yards in 13 plays to pull within five. They had a chance to win it after a brief four-play Giants drive.

But then New York did something it failed too so many times a season ago. It slammed the door shut.

As long as Harbaugh roams New York's sideline, the Giants will be more physical, or as physical, as the other team. They'll have the stamina and mental endurance to go 15 rounds. They'll be prepared -- an alien concept in East Rutherford. The three, four moments that dictate the outcome of close games will go in their direction.

It was first-and-goal for the Titans at the Giants seven yard line with 24 seconds left when Ward flushed left. This pass last year finds Wan'Dale Robinson , or Carnell Tate or Calvin Ridley . The Giants blew double-digit, fourth-quarter leads five times in 2025.

But this one didn't. Holland knew, with Ward headed left in a scramble drill, receivers would follow. Holland held his position at the middle of the field and drifted with Ward. Holland readied to come up if Ward ran. When Holland saw Ward cock his arm, Holland held firm.

The ball floated. Holland jumped. Game over.

"The ball is just coming my way," said Holland, who now has a league-leading three interceptions this season.

The Giants have the Cardinals next week. Then the Commanders, who may still be without quarterback Jayden Daniels . Both games are winnable following the script they deployed against the Titans.

It will get harder down the stretch when the competition stiffens. The same could be said in 2022, when the Giants took down the Lamar Jackson -led Ravens, the Aaron Rodgers -led Packers , and eventually the Vikings in the first round of the playoffs.

They'll add another quarterback to the room -- either by trade ( J.J. McCarthy ) or free agency ( Jimmy Garoppolo ) -- this week in case Winston falters. But this season is not lost -- not yet. The Giants showed on Sunday they're going to fight.

"This is what it's all about," Harbaugh said. "Finding a way to win a rough game."

They don't care if it's pretty. They just want to find ways to win.

articles.title: Bengals' revamped defense regresses against Steelers as Cincinnati falls short of 3-0 start
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals and their overhauled defense certainly looked the part during the season's first two weeks.  A Steelers offense that had managed one t...
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH (AP) — The Cincinnati Bengals and their overhauled defense certainly looked the part during the season's first two weeks.

The defense unraveled quickly — and repeatedly — in a 30-27 loss to Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

A Steelers offense that had managed one touchdown during the season's first eight quarters found the end zone three times and rolled up 411 yards against defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence and the rest of a revamped unit that played with swagger during Cincinnati's unbeaten start.

Rodgers picked apart the Bengals secondary and the Lawrence-led defensive line that looked so dangerous in opening wins over Tampa Bay and Houston allowed Steelers running back Jaylen Warren to compile 176 yards, including 127 on the ground.

"It wasn't us," said Lawrence, who had both of Cincinnati's sacks. "We know we can't allow that."

The Bengals, who forced four turnovers in a Week 1 win over Tampa Bay and held C.J. Stroud and Houston without a touchdown in Week 2, were gashed repeatedly by a new-look Pittsburgh offensive line that included rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor at right tackle and a banged-up Warren gaining yards in chunks for a 7.5-per-carry average.

Not that Lawrence, whose arrival in a trade with the Giants in April signaled that Cincinnati was finally getting serious about shoring up one of the league's worst defenses, was impressed.

"I think a lot of what was going on was self-inflicted," Lawrence said. "I mean, you watched the game. You know what happened. I don't think it was anything special they had going on. We just didn't do well on our end."

Pittsburgh scored on each of its first three possessions and was at midfield on its fourth when Rodgers' pass glanced off the hands of wide receiver Roman Wilson and into the arms of safety Jordan Battle .

The Steelers punted just twice. A third was nullified by the first of two crucial special-teams errors when Cincinnati's Cedric Johnson was called for roughing Pittsburgh punter Cameron Johnston , extending a drive that ended with a touchdown pass from Rodgers to DK Metcalf .

Cincinnati later gifted the Steelers a field goal when punt returner Ke'Shawn Williams let the ball smack off his facemask.

Coach Zac Taylor spread the blame around and declined to get into specifics about how Cincinnati's defense turned back the clock, and not in a good way.

"I don't want to pinpoint it right now," he said. "We'll watch the tape and have a better answer for you tomorrow."

The review session won't be pretty, especially on Pittsburgh's last drive. The Bengals caught a break when a 80-plus yard run by Warren was called back due to a holding penalty. The Steelers raced into scoring position anyway, thanks in large part to a 47-yard catch-and-run by 6-foot-7, 300-plus-pound tight end Darnell Washington , who shrugged off a couple of tackles before thundering down the sideline.

"We've got to do a better job of getting the stop there," Taylor said. "I thought we pinned them down in there, gave ourselves a chance. We have to stop, get the ball back."

They eventually did, but only after the Steelers took the lead. Joe Burrow , who was nearly flawless while passing for 282 yards and three scores, get the Bengals to the fringe of field-goal range before getting strip-sacked in the final minute.

Just like that, a chance for the team's first 3-0 start since 2015 was gone.

"We own it," Lawrence said. "We know who we are. We're still champions."

Maybe by the middle of January. But not yet.

articles.title: Jackson Koivun proves captain's pick was right with unbeaten Presidents Cup debut
articles.summary: After being a controversial pick, Jackson Koivun went undefeated to help the U.S. win the Presidents Cup.
articles.body:
Jackson Koivun was seemingly twirling his club and chasing his golf ball before he ever finished his swing.

If there was any doubt where the confidence level of the 21-year-old making his Presidents Cup debut was, his tee shot on the par-4 18th hole at Medinah No. 3 put it all to rest. Koivun's club twirled with swagger, and he had a bounce down the fairway like a golfer striding toward a blowout victory in a major championship.

It would've been impossible to tell, not knowing the situation, he had a 1-up lead against the International team's best player with one hole to go.

As if the tee shot wasn't filled with confidence, Koivun's club twirl after his approach could've spun up a tornado it was so violent. Koivun hit his approach to 8 feet, and after Kim missed his birdie look, the duo took off their hats and shook hands.

Koivun came into the 16th Presidents Cup as a controversial captain's selection, but what Koivun did on Sunday proved Brandt Snedeker made the right decision. Koivun won his singles match, 2 up, and was the only American to go undefeated at Medinah, earning 2½ points in three matches as the U.S. had a historic, come-from-behind victory to win its 11th straight Presidents Cup.

And for Koivun, as if everything he has done since turning professional three months ago wasn't enough, his stellar victory Sunday proved he has arrived as a major force in professional golf with a good chance to be a stalwart donning the red, white and blue in international team competitions for years to come.

Presidents Cup 2026: Best photos from Sunday singles at Medinah

"It's just been such a cool learning experience," Koivun said Sunday. "Being under captain Snedeker and being around all these guys is so cool, and obviously to come out on top after a large deficit coming into today is just a feeling I can't explain."

Koivun stood on the 11th tee facing a 2-down deficit but proceeded to win the next three holes and four of the next six. Even after losing the 16th, Koivun made a par on the 17th and then proceeded to hit two of the most confident shots of his life when the lights were the brightest.

Koivun's selection was unprecedented but well deserved. Last year, as the No. 1 amateur in the world, Koivun went 3-1-0 in the 50th Walker Cup, including winning both of his singles matches. Then, he was 1 up with one to play against now-No. 1 amateur Preston Stout in the semifinals when Auburn clinched the match. The next day, he won his match to help Auburn win its second national championship in three years.

Then in his third professional start, Koivun won the 3M Open on the PGA Tour. Last week, he finished T-5 at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.

And this week, he was the breakout start for the USA.

"I had some goals, but for it to come this quickly is definitely shocking, and I'm just thankful and grateful for the trust the captains put in me to put me out in three of the five matches," Koivun said.

Cameron Young and Chris Gotterup were also making their President Cup debuts for the Americans, with both players earning three points each. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler, who was runner-up to Koivun at the 3M, also earned three points. But those were the only golfers to earn more than Koivun did.

Koivun's performance is not surprising to those who have followed his amateur career. His resume pits him as one of, if not, the best amateurs this century. That quick transition to the professional game was almost a given, and now with even more experience and confidence under his belt, it's likely his trajectory is only going to go upward.

And if the leadership of team golf in the U.S. has its way, Koivun will be a fixture of future Presidents and Ryder Cup teams for years and years to come.

"I think I'll just take a lot of knowledge that I can be out here and I can compete," Koivun said. "It's just exciting being able to call these guys my friends, and now when I go to tournaments it's not like, oh, there's so and so. It's like, I was on a team with them, and we won the Presidents Cup."

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

The regular season has officially ended, and now the fun can begin for the Red Sox . Boston 's journey to a World Series win starts on Tuesday with the Wild Card series against the Yankees .

Last season, the Red Sox faced the Yankees in their first playoff appearance since 2021. After beating New York in the Wild Card game that year, the Yankees won the series last season, 2-1.

A historic rivalry, the Red Sox and Yankees exchanged wins and losses this year, from close games to blowouts. Who has the edge when they compete for a chance to advance?

The Yankees finalized their rotation, hoping those players can shut down the Red Sox. Here's a breakdown of the Yankees' starters they will send to the mound to face Boston in the playoffs.

Who will start for Yankees in Wild Card series against Red Sox?

On Tuesday, September 29 , Cam Schlittler will start for the Yankees.

A top contender for the AL Cy Young, Schlittler's 2026 saw the following: a 14-6 record, a 1.95 ERA, and 239 strikeouts. In four outings against Boston this season, Schlittler went 2-1 with a 0.74 ERA while striking out 27 batters.

On Wednesday, September 30 , Max Fried will get the start.

Fried missed two months of the season with an elbow injury and later had a bone bruise in his left elbow. He had a 5-5 record with a 2.80 ERA this season. In two games against Boston, he went 1-0 with a 0.77 ERA while striking out 13 batters.

If necessary, the Yankees will start Gerrit Cole on Thursday, October 1 .

articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are 2-1 after beating the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The two straight wins have saved Deshaun Watson 's job as starting quarterback and completely changed the mood in the stands. Watson was being booed during the preseason, but now they're chanting his name .

Of course, that doesn't necessarily mean all Browns fans are in a good mood these days. Take the people in this video for instance. There was a serious disagreement that led to a fan in a Nick Chubb jersey throwing punches with another fan in a Shedeur Sanders jersey.

Welp fight right by me. Go browns 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/xQvXCehho9 — byron (@TheSimbaPikachu) September 27, 2026

Welp fight right by me. Go browns 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/xQvXCehho9

byron (@TheSimbaPikachu) September 27, 2026

The fight was broken up by other fans and luckily there was a fan wearing a Luke Kuechley jersey there to protect the fan wearing a Tua Tagovailoa jersey. Just your typical scene in the crowd at an NFL game.

Watson completed 16-of-30 passes for 144 yards and two touchdowns. His main target was Harold Fannin Jr. a tight end who finished with seven catches for 51 yards and caught both touchdown passes. Watson also had to run 11 times and had 45 yards on the ground.

The Browns only loss of the season came against the Jacksonville Jaguars who beat the Patriots even more convincingly than they beat the Browns in Week 1. Cleveland might actually be decent as long as Watson continues to protect the football.

Cleveland will now have a short week to prepare for the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. The Steelers are also 2-1 so whoever wins the game will wake up in first place in the AFC North on Friday morning.

articles.title: 49ers injury nightmare continues with Mike Evans, Trent Williams joining laundry list of banged-up players
articles.summary: Here's a look at the latest injuries for San Francisco.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have had serious injury issues over the last few seasons, and that only continued in their Week 3 game vs. the Arizona Cardinals .

As the 49ers built a big lead at home vs. Arizona, the team saw several of their most important players go down with injuries. That is on top of the injuries that the 49ers have already experienced this season, which includes a handful of their wide receivers.

While the 49ers continue on into this season, they will once again have to weather these injuries with their depth. Here's a look at the latest injuries for San Francisco .

Despite a strong performance against the Cardinals, the 49ers suffered more injuries to pile onto their already long injury report. Most notable was wide receiver Mike Evans , who needed to be carted off the field after he suffered a ribs injury. Evans looked to be in some significant pain as he was walking off the field initially.

Evans was ultimately diagnosed with a rib strain, which will require more evaluation after the game.

After Evans left, it was left tackle Trent Williams who needed medical assistance next. Williams was diagnosed with a stinger and was declared questionable to return to the game, but not before he also was carted to the locker room.

Williams' injury appeared to occur on a Christian McCaffrey rushing touchdown.

On defense, cornerback Deommodore Lenoir was taken out of the game to undergo a concussion evaluation. A concussion would force him to not only miss the rest of the game, but he would also be put into concussion protocol.

These injuries are just the latest in San Francisco' injury-riddled season. The 49ers have already seen key players like Ricky Pearsall , D'Zhaun Stribling and Nick Bosa suffer injuries that will keep them out for varying degrees of time.

articles.title: Patriots news: Is Drake Maye's shoulder a reason behind poor play? Here's what he said
articles.summary: Drake Maye’s dreadful start to the 2026 NFL season continues as the New England Patriots suffered an embarrassing 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Su...
articles.body:
Drake Maye 's dreadful start to the 2026 NFL season continues as the New England Patriots suffered an embarrassing 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday afternoon.

Maye is going through the third season of his career with the Patriots . He enjoyed a breakout year in Year 2, leading New England to Super Bowl 60 before losing to the Seattle Seahawks .

Things have been brutal for Maye since that success last year. Maye only completed 14 out of 25 passes for 199 yards, then committed two interceptions and a fumble.

Speculation surfaced about his shoulder , which he injured in the AFC Championship game against the Denver Broncos . Reporters asked him about his shoulder, which he made an effort to reassure them that it's not in bad condition.

"Unacceptable," Maye stated upon starting his presser, per reporter Mike Reiss. "You're gonna get banged up every now and then, but at the same time, a lot of guys are banged up. So looking forward to get back to playing winning football. That's the main thing, and knowing that I play a big role in that, and then taking that and taking the bull by its horns,"

"I wouldn't say there's a problem with my shoulder. I think there's times where I think you look back on the playoff run in that Denver game when I took the hit. Now I feel good here in training camp and continue to let it loose. "

The Patriots need Drake Maye to return to star form. His performances to start the campaign have been far from the games he delivered last year, needing his struggles to be a major wake-up call for the young quarterback.

Maye only has one passing touchdown to his name after three games. He has largely struggled with six interceptions, emphasizing how slow New England has been to begin the season.

The Patriots will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being on the road. They gear up for division rivalry clash with the Buffalo Bills on Oct. 4 at 1 p.m. ET.

Three plays before he exited, the six-time Pro Bowl selection did take a big hit from safety Budda Baker on a 9-yard reception. After grabbing his right side, Evans was in obvious discomfort as he walked slowly off the field. He briefly took a knee when he reached the sideline and appeared to be trying to catch his breath. He took a seat on the bench while surrounded by members of the medical staff and a cart was summoned.

Robinson (ankle) was carted off in Week 2 after Stribling (ankle) did so in the season opener. Both Robinson and Stribling are on injured reserve. Without Evans, the 49ers' four remaining active wideouts are Deebo Samuel , Jacob Cowing , Jordan Watkins and KhaDarel Hodge .

articles.title: He was the first-ever player to win a match at the Laver Cup nine years ago
articles.summary: The 2026 Laver Cup has concluded. Team Europe secured victory following Alexander Zverev’s victory over Learner Tien, triumphing 7-6, 6-3. The occasion repre...
articles.body:
Team Europe secured victory following Alexander Zverev's victory over Learner Tien, triumphing 7-6, 6-3.

The occasion represents Team Europe's sixth Laver Cup title and its second triumph in three years.

The event was first won by Team Europe in 2017. The team in blue triumphed 15-9 following inspired performances by Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal .

Neither of these players were the first to win a match at the high-profile exhibition event.

Cilic , the 2014 US Open champion, became the first player to win a match at the Laver Cup when he defeated Frances Tiafoe at the 2017 event.

The Croatian star, who also reached the 2017 Wimbledon final and 2018 Australian Open final, defeated Tiafoe 7-6, 7-6 at the O2 Arena in Prague, Czech Republic.

The result secured Team Europe their first-ever point at the event.

Cilic also competed in doubles alongside 2010 Wimbledon finalist Tomas Berdych.

The Croatian-Czech duo were defeated by Frances Tiafoe and Jack Sock, 6-7, 6-7.

The result had little effect on the outcome, as Team Europe went on to claim a 15-9 victory.

Following the 2026 Laver Cup, Team Europe leads Team World 6-3 overall.

How did Roger Federer react after securing Team Europe's 2017 Laver Cup victory?

Federer, a 20-time major champion, stunned Nick Kyrgios at the 2017 Laver Cup to secure Team Europe's first-ever victory.

The Swiss superstar roared back from a significant deficit to defeat the Australian 4-6 7-6(6) 11-9.

Federer was 5-8 down in the tiebreak and saved a match point at 8-9.

"I was ready to go – I had to be. That's what a team member does," Federer said afterwards, as per the Laver Cup website.

"The boys played fantastic all weekend, but we knew it could change very quickly on Sunday.

"The Team World boys have been great, in the doubles especially, and we knew it was going to be tough.

"I was looking at getting ready for a doubles at the very end. I'm very pleased and relieved that we did win the singles and got it done."

Federer won three matches at the 2017 event, picking up seven points for Team Europe.

Federer also defeated Sam Querrey in singles and combined with Rafael Nadal to defeat Querrey and Jack Sock in doubles.

Five years later, Federer played his final competitive tennis match alongside Rafael Nadal at the 2022 Laver Cup.

Sock and Frances Tiafoe defeated the iconic duo 4-6 7-6 11-9.

articles.title: Andy Murray confirms if he still plans to coach Jack Draper next year
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Andy Murray returned to coaching for the first time since his split with Novak Djokovic, joining compatriot Jack Draper’s team. Amid an...
articles.body:
Earlier this year, Andy Murray returned to coaching for the first time since his split with Novak Djokovic, joining compatriot Jack Draper's team.

Amid an injury-ridden season, Draper hired Murray ahead of the grass swing, with the two having their first tournament together at the Eastbourne Open. There, the 24-year-old Briton reached the semifinals before falling to Ugo Humbert.

But Draper's momentum was halted after he was forced to withdraw from Wimbledon with a recurring left-arm injury. He attempted a comeback during the North American swing, but suffered first-round exits in both Montreal and Cincinnati before officially announcing on social media that he won't play for the remainder of the 2026 season.

Andy Murray speaks about his future coaching Jack Draper

There was never any indication that Murray would be Draper's long-term coach when he initially joined his team in May. But now, the 39-year-old Scot has confirmed he intends to stay in the role next season.

"There's still plans to help him [Draper]," Murray told Sky Sports . "I don't know where that is. I'm not entirely sure because his ranking will have dropped. I don't know if he would get into Australia and potentially relying on wild cards and things like that, so we'll see.

"Hopefully he'll be back on the court training again soon and getting ready for the new season – it has been an interesting year. I've been doing a little bit of coaching, which I've enjoyed, but also Jack's had a few injuries and has been off the tour for quite a while, so I haven't been able to get into that quite as much as I would have liked.

"I do still enjoy coming and watching [tennis] a little bit, but I'm happy doing what I'm doing with my kids just now." Since retiring from tennis at the 2024 Paris Olympics, Murray has had brief coaching stints with Djokovic and now Draper, but has admitted he is content being away from the sport.

Draper's ranking has plummeted to 155th in the world due to his injury struggles, after being as high as fourth last season. Outside of the Eastbourne Open, Draper's best result was a quarterfinal finish at the Indian Wells Open, where he picked up a win over Djokovic.

This season, Draper has featured at seven tour-level competitions, with a win-loss record of 8-7. His ranking means he will have to rely on receiving a wildcard to play in the main draw of the 2027 Australian Open, or come through qualifying.

His fall in the rankings also saw him lose British number one status, which now belongs to Wimbledon semifinalist Arthur Fery. There are now five British players on the ATP Tour ranked higher than Draper.

articles.title: Braves at Marlins series recap: It’s onto October for Atlanta
articles.summary: The Braves take a Fall jaunt to South Beach before rocking and rolling into the Postseason
articles.body:
The regular season is over and it ended in quiet fashion for the Atlanta Braves . All of their big fireworks and celebrations took place last Sunday when they picked up a sweep in Houston in order to clinch the NL East title. It's been a week since then and the Braves have essentially been in a bit of a holding pattern as they prepare for what will hopefully be a long and deep run into the Postseason.

Before they could get there, they had to play out the string and finish off the season with a road trip to Miami. The Marlins were playing to at least avoid having a losing season and while that may not seem like a lot, it means a lot to the players and the fans down there so there was certainly a bit more energy coming from the Marlins' dugout rather than what we saw from the Braves. I'm not complaining, though — I think we'd all much rather see the Braves empty the tank over a long Postseason run rather than doing it in a season-ending series in Miami with not much on the line. Let's take a look at the final series of the regular season, shall we?

Shout-out to Eury Pérez . If you're going to end your season, you may as well go out with a banger. Pérez did just that, as he ended up throwing a complete game, one-hit shutout on 105 pitches, eight strikeouts and just one walk. As far as Pérez goes, that's a nice bit of redemption for him after the Braves really roughed him up in their last encounter and it was a bit of lovely moment for Marlins fans since it was the 10-year anniversary of former Marlins star José Fernández passing away.

As you can suspect from the results that I just described, there wasn't a lot to write home about from Atlanta's perspective. Sean Murphy got the lone hit and there didn't seem like there was much urgency going on — which is understandable considering that Atlanta was already locked into the three-seed and the Wild Card Series before this series even began.

Anyways, Ray Kerr pitched three shutout innings and Grant Holmes tossed four innings while only giving up three hits and a run. He did walk three batters as well, so he did have to deal with some real traffic while he was out there. Still, it's a pretty solid performance and one that hopefully Holmes can build on as the BRaves enter the Postseason.

This one was all Braves from nearly the words "Play Ball." After Matt Olson got things going with a sacrifice fly in the first inning (that Michael Harris II did a great job of scoring on from a very shallow fly ball), the Braves added three more in the second inning thanks to a two-run dinger from Dominic Smith and an error allowing Ha-Seong Kim to score on an infield grounder from Ronald Acuña Jr. that Javier Sanoja booted into the air.

From the second inning onwards, the Braves maintained a pretty comfortable lead. An RBI double from Money Mike and an RBI single from Matt Olson made it 6-0 Braves in the fourth inning. While the Marlins did add on a pair of runs to make it on the board in their half of the fourth and then later on cut it down to a three-run lead with a Heriberto Hernández triple off of Robert Suarez in the seventh inning, the Braves got two of those runs back in the ninth after Drake Baldwin went deep to bring us to the final score of 8-3.

If this was a rehearsal for a bullpen game then the Braves looked pretty solid in that regard. Brent Suter went three innings while only giving up a hit, Victor Mederos went two innings where the only baserunner he had to deal with came via a walk and both Dylan Lee and Raisel Iglesias pitched scoreless innings as well. Dylan Dodd got knocked around for a couple of runs and Robert Suarez got ambushed once again but none of that was overly concerning to see. The bullpen is going to have to come up huge in October if the Braves are going to go far and so far, the outlook is encouraging.

I'd imagine that more eyes across Braves Country were focused on what was happening in Philadelphia and San Diego rather than what was happening in Miami. In the end, the Phillies finally punched their ticket to October after finally picking up the win that they'd needed for what felt like this entire week and the Diamondbacks ended up not even keeping up their end of the bargain, anyways. The Braves will be taking on the Phillies, which I'm sure everybody is s u p e r e x c i t e d to see happen once again.

Anyways, the last dress rehearsal for the Braves saw them go down in defeat in order to finish their season with 94 wins. If this was JR Ritchie's audition for a Wild Card roster spot, I'd say that the good news is that he did end up eating nearly six innings. The bad news is that he got knocked around for seven hits, two walks and four runs scored while only striking out two batters, so the results weren't exactly encouragin. We'll see what happens as far as his roster status goes but if they're going by results then it's really anybody's guess as to whether or not he'll make it onto the roster.

AJ Smith-Shawver followed that up by giving up a long homer to Griffin Conine in the seventh inning, which was his only blemish across 1.1 innings. Elieser Hernández ended up pitching the final ining this season for the Braves, which is good for him considering the up-and-down nature of call-ups that he's head to deal with over the course of this season.

Meanwhile, a patchwork lineup didn't exactly make a ton of noise and if you were expecting anything different, I don't know what to tell you. Mauricio Dubón did hit one out in the third inning and then he added on an RBI single later on, so he had a solid day. DaShawn Keirsey Jr. picked up his first (and only) RBI of the season on a productive out and Sean Murphy had two hits. That's about it for Atlanta's offense and the Braves went quietly into the Postseason.

So there you have it! If you care about results, then the Braves aren't exactly rolling into the Postseason as they dropped consecutive series against the Reds and Marlins to finish off the final week of the season. With that being said, I'd imagine that everybody has had their eyes on the Postseason (and the Wild Card Series in particular) ever since they had the champagne shower in Houston seven days ago, so this wasn't exactly a week that called for much urgency from the Braves.

The good news is that they didn't have to expend anywhere near the energy or resources that their Wild Card Series opponents in Philadelphia had to pour out in order to just make the Postseason, so the Braves will have the advantage of being able to set themselves up for potential success rather than essentially having to come into the Postseason battle-scarred. Philadelphia's situation honestly reminds me of how the Braves had to play all 162 games in order to make the Wild Card Series in 2024 and we all know how that ended for Atlanta once they had to travel to San Diego after a tough and trying week. The Phillies will have to ifgure out a way to navigate similar circumstances and it's Atlanta's job to make sure that an exhausted-looking Phillies squad looks as such once the Wild Card Series starts on Tuesday.

Overall, it's been a pretty interesting season overall! We all hoped that the Braves would be in this position and a lot of the projection models predicted that the Braves would be where they're at right now. As Ivan has mentioned a bunch of times now, they surely took a roundabout route to get to those 94 wins and a NL East divisional title but they made it there and now they will try their best in the crapshoot that is the MLB Postseason. The Braves will get one day of rest before playing in front of what will hopefully be an energetic and loud crowd at Truist Park for the first Postseason game in this ballpark since 2023. Truist Park has been a place of comfort for the Braves so far this season and now they'll have the benefit of playing this Wild Card Series all at home with a shot to go even further. We'll see what happens!

articles.title: South Carolina star EDGE will be out against Kentucky Wildcats
articles.summary: The Kentucky Wildcats will face the South Carolina Gamecocks this upcoming weekend, and their opponent will be short one of its star players.
articles.body:
The Kentucky Wildcats will get a huge boost on Saturday as they'll face the South Carolina Gamecocks , who will be short one of their best defensive players.

That stud is Dylan Stewart, who is among the best defensive ends in the conference. Stewart is a 6-foot-6 EDGE rusher, who had 12 tackles for a loss and 4.5 sacks a season ago. The junior is expected to be one of the top defensive players in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Cats were going to be a heavy favorite anyway, now ranked as the 24th-best team in the country via the AP Poll.

Why is Stewart going to miss time? Well, on a play with multiple flags, he threw a punch against Alabama, a game that got out of control early with the Crimson Tide destroying South Carolina. Alabama ended up winning 49-18 and took a 35-10 lead into the half. While there's no excuse, emotions were undoubtedly high.

"I saw the play that he got the penalty on. I didn't see it until just now, and that's unacceptable. That's not how we do things around here. I'm embarrassed to see that because that's not what we're about. Didn't see it during the game. I knew we had a penalty. I didn't know what happened. We've got a lot of fiery, emotional, competitive guys, and I love that. When you're in the arena, emotions are high," South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer said following the game via Kentucky Sports Radio's Jack Pilgrim .

Stewart should still be a top pick in next year's draft. He has the frame to be a monster at the NFL level and has had double-digit tackles for loss in two straight seasons. The talent is undoubtedly there.

Thankfully for head coach Will Stein, that's one less problem he'll have to plan for Saturday. Kickoff is set for 4:15 p.m. ET and will be at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia.

articles.title: SA vs AUS 2nd ODI: David Miller, Temba Bavuma tons help South Africa take unassailable 2-0 lead over Australia
articles.summary: David Miller and Temba Bavuma hit centuries as South Africa beat Australia by 32 runs in the second ODI on Sunday to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the thr...
articles.body:
David Miller and Temba Bavuma hit centuries as South Africa beat Australia by 32 runs in the second ODI on Sunday to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Miller smashed 142 off 93 balls for his eighth ODI century, while Bavuma made 103 for his sixth hundred in the format. Their knocks helped South Africa post 365-9. Australia's Jack Edwards, playing only his second ODI, took 5-67, while Josh Hazlewood claimed 3-70. Hazlewood had also dismissed Aiden Markram for a first-ball duck.

Australia again chose to chase after winning the toss but were bowled out for 333 in the final over. Captain Mitchell Marsh and Travis Head gave Australia a strong start, putting together 130 runs in 17 overs. Marsh made 84, while Head also scored 84. But South Africa's spinners changed the game in the middle overs. Keshav Maharaj took 2-54 and Markram picked up 1-55 as Bavuma made full use of his 30 overs of spin. Xavier Bartlett provided some late resistance with 50 off 28 balls, including 19 runs from Bjorn Fortuin's final over. Fortuin finished with 2-70.

The result followed South Africa's 67-run win in the first ODI in Durban and gave them the series with one match still to play. The second ODI was also the annual Pink Day fixture, which raises money for cancer research and treatment. Miller wore his mother Jenny's name on the back of his jersey. She is a breast cancer survivor. Australia have not won a bilateral ODI series against South Africa since 2014. The visitors will now look to avoid a clean sweep when the teams meet in the final ODI on Wednesday.
